children: Mirendil has raised $1 billion in a Series A funding round led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital.

San Francisco-based Mirendil makes artificial-intelligence systems that are geared toward the biology and medical fields. The tools it builds are meant to make AI-driven research and development more accessible to scientists and engineers.
Battery Ventures, Doer Capital, Gil & Co., Google, M13, Pear VC and S32 all participated in the round as well, Mirendil said Thursday.
The company plans to use the funding from the new round to continue development of its models.
In recent results, Mirendil showed that one researcher working with AI agents was able to pretrain its coding model Mirendil-Base in three and a half months with less than $10 million in compute.
Lor, another product now in private beta mode, would offer hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days at a time.
